bug_description.original: The ZMTP v1 static allocator in the code is needlessly resized. Resizing the static allocator is unnecessary because it is fixed, unlike the shared allocator which can take the message buffer for zero copy.
bug_description.normalized: In the staged vulnerable checkout `061ce6cea15b4e2aee9bea977902f8201a5f7a41`, the unversioned ZMTP/1.0 handshake path selected by `_greeting_recv[9] & 0x01 == 0` constructs `v1_decoder_t` on top of `c_single_allocator`, whose constructor allocates one fixed 8192-byte `_buf` but whose `resize()` method still overwrites `_buf_size`. The exact staged witness begins `ff 00 00 00 00 00 00 c8 00 00`, so `receive_greeting()` marks the peer unversioned, `one_byte_size_ready()` takes the long-frame branch, and `eight_byte_size_ready()` decodes the first payload length as `51200`, hence `msg_size = 51199`. Large body reads therefore use the zero-copy `get_buffer()` path; after each such read `in_event_internal()` copies the read count into `_insize`, calls `_decoder->resize_buffer(_insize)`, and `decoder_base_t::decode()` subtracts the consumed chunk from `_to_read`. Because `c_single_allocator::resize()` blindly stores the last body-read length in `_buf_size`, one prior `8215`-byte read makes the allocator advertise 8215 bytes while `_buf` is still the original 8192-byte allocation. Once later zero-copy progress leaves the same frame's remaining tail smaller than 8215, `get_buffer()` falls back to `_buf` but still returns size 8215, and `tcp_read()` passes that mismatched pair into `recv`. Stage 01 saved an AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow `WRITE of size 8215` at that `recv` call, and the patch fixes the bug by making `c_single_allocator::resize()` a no-op.

source.description: First project parser statement on the vulnerable path that turns attacker-controlled greeting bytes into the dispatch state selecting the unversioned ZMTP/1.0 decoder backed by the static allocator.
source.value_from: The staged witness is the 59424-byte file `gt_results/arvo_21984/poc`, whose first 10 bytes are exactly `ff 00 00 00 00 00 00 c8 00 00`. After `receive_greeting()` has read those 10 bytes into `_greeting_recv`, byte 9 is `0x00`, so this condition is true and `unversioned` becomes true.

tainted_value_origin.code: sent = send (server_accept, (const char *) data, size, MSG_NOSIGNAL);
tainted_value_origin.description: The harness streams the exact `poc` bytes over a TCP connection to the accepted server socket; libzmq later reads that same byte stream through its ZMTP engine.

sink.code: const ssize_t rc = recv (s_, static_cast<char *> (data_), size_, 0);
sink.description: Exact project sink just above the ASan interceptor. It passes the fixed allocator buffer pointer together with the corrupted logical size into `recv`.
sink.note: In the saved crash, `data_` aliases the 8192-byte `_buf` allocated for `c_single_allocator`, while `size_` is 8215. AddressSanitizer therefore reports `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 8215` in `recv`, with `zmq::tcp_read` at this line as the first project frame.

root_cause.description: The static v1 allocator overwrites its advertised size with the last read count even though its backing `_buf` is a fixed heap allocation created once in the constructor.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes only this statement, making `resize()` a no-op for the fixed allocator. In the vulnerable build it can store `8215` into `_buf_size` while `_buf` remains the original 8192-byte allocation.

parser_admitted.condition: The first size byte available to the v1 decoder is `0xff`, so `one_byte_size_ready()` takes the long-frame branch and schedules `eight_byte_size_ready()`. This is the only executed parse path that can produce the later `payload_length = 51200` and `msg_size = 51199`.

coarse_trace.summary: The 10th greeting byte is parsed as an unversioned-protocol marker, so libzmq selects the ZMTP/1.0 handshake that will build the fixed-buffer v1 decoder.
The unversioned handshake constructs `v1_decoder_t` with `c_single_allocator`, whose fixed `_buf` is allocated at the default `in_batch_size` of 8192 bytes.
The decoder parses the witness long-frame length as 51200, derives `msg_size = 51199`, and `flags_ready()` schedules body reads from `_in_progress.data()` with `_to_read = 51199`.

Large body reads use the zero-copy path; one earlier 8215-byte read is stored in `_insize`, forwarded through `resize_buffer()`, and then consumed by `decoder_base_t::decode()` so the remaining tail eventually drops below the stale allocator size.
A later fallback `get_buffer()` call returns the original 8192-byte `_buf` together with the stale logical size 8215, and `recv` overruns the heap buffer.

fine_trace.note: After 10 greeting bytes have been read, the low bit of byte 9 is zero for the staged witness, so this check marks the peer unversioned. That dispatch selects the ZMTP/1.0 handshake path that later instantiates the vulnerable static allocator.

The unversioned handshake constructs `v1_decoder_t` on `c_single_allocator`. `_options.in_batch_size` defaults to 8192, and the saved ASan allocation stack shows `c_single_allocator::c_single_allocator` mallocs a single 8192-byte `_buf` for this decoder.

Because `one_byte_size_ready()` saw the leading size byte `0xff`, this function parses the next eight witness bytes `00 00 00 00 00 00 c8 00` as `payload_length = 51200`. The zero-length, max-message-size, and `size_t`-range guards in this function do not reject that value.

depends_on.via: the v1 decoder receives the already-read greeting bytes

fine_trace.note: Subtracting the flags byte converts the accepted long-frame payload length into `msg_size = 51199`, the body length that exceeds the fixed allocator size of 8192.
After `init_size (msg_size)` succeeds and the witness flags byte `0x00` is stored, `flags_ready()` points `_read_pos` at the message body storage and sets `_to_read = _in_progress.size() = 51199`.

With `_to_read = 51199` and the static allocator still reporting 8192, `get_buffer()` takes the large-message zero-copy branch and asks the caller to read directly into `_read_pos` instead of the allocator buffer `_buf`.

depends_on.via: the decoder's fixed allocator size is 8192

fine_trace.note: On one earlier zero-copy body read, `read (_inpos, bufsize)` returns 8215 bytes, so this assignment stores `_insize = 8215`. The later crashing `size_ = 8215` shows such a read occurred, because this read-count state is what the engine propagates into the allocator.
Immediately after that body read, the stream engine forwards the 8215-byte `_insize` value into the decoder allocator state.

Root cause. The fixed allocator copies `new_size_` into `_buf_size`, so the prior 8215-byte body read changes the logical allocator size to 8215 even though the backing `_buf` is still the original 8192-byte heap allocation from step 2.

Because the body read used the zero-copy destination from step 6 (`data_ == _read_pos`), `decode()` consumes that same 8215-byte chunk without copying, advances `_read_pos`, and reduces `_to_read` by 8215. Repeated executions of this zero-copy update on the same message eventually leave the remaining tail smaller than the stale allocator size 8215.

depends_on.via: data_ == _read_pos in the zero-copy decode branch

fine_trace.note: When a later call sees `_to_read < _allocator.size ()`, `get_buffer()` falls through to the static allocator buffer. `_buf` is still the original 8192-byte allocation from step 2, but `_allocator.size()` now reports 8215 because of step 9, so this branch returns an oversized `(data, size)` pair for the next socket read.

fine_trace.code: const ssize_t rc = recv (s_, static_cast<char *> (data_), size_, 0);
fine_trace.note: Sink. `data_` now aliases the fixed allocator buffer from step 11 while `size_` is 8215, so `recv` writes past the 8192-byte region allocated for `c_single_allocator`. This matches the saved AddressSanitizer `WRITE of size 8215` and the crash stack `recv -> zmq::tcp_read -> zmq::stream_engine_base_t::read`.

allocation_context.note: The saved ASan report says the bad write lands 0 bytes to the right of the 8192-byte region allocated here. `options.cpp:247` sets the default `in_batch_size` to 8192, which `handshake_v1_0_unversioned()` passes into `v1_decoder_t` on this path.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: Parsed from staged `default_crash_trace.txt` / `sanitizer_trace.txt`; cross-checked against the vulnerable source read from the running ARVO workspace container at `/src/libzmq` (commit `061ce6cea15b4e2aee9bea977902f8201a5f7a41`) and the staged fix in `patch.diff`.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved ASan trace reports `recv` as the runtime crash location and names `zmq::tcp_read` at `src/tcp.cpp:299` as the first project frame, which is the exact sink recorded here.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. The patch changes only `c_single_allocator::resize()`, and the saved allocation stack shows the backing buffer is still the constructor's fixed 8192-byte allocation. This is the only source location that can make that fixed buffer later be advertised as 8215.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved crash stack `recv -> zmq::tcp_read -> zmq::stream_engine_base_t::read -> zmq::stream_engine_base_t::in_event_internal` matches fine-trace steps 11-12 and the vulnerable `get_buffer` / `resize_buffer` / `decode` logic in steps 6-10.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The witness's 10th greeting byte selects the unversioned v1 static-allocator path, the long-frame prefix and eight-byte length produce `msg_size = 51199`, one prior 8215-byte zero-copy body read is copied into `_buf_size`, and later zero-copy progress reduces `_to_read` so fallback `get_buffer()` passes the fixed `_buf` to `recv` with size 8215.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `docker exec gt-arvo_21984-workspace /bin/bash -lc '/bin/arvo run'`, which fed `gt_results/arvo_21984/poc` to `/out/test_connect_null_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 8215 in recv`, with project stack `zmq::tcp_read -> zmq::stream_engine_base_t::read -> zmq::stream_engine_base_t::in_event_internal` and allocation stack reaching `zmq::c_single_allocator`.

format.contract: The exact staged witness is the 59424-byte file `gt_results/arvo_21984/poc`. Its first 10 bytes are exactly `ff 00 00 00 00 00 00 c8 00 00`, so `receive_greeting()` sets `unversioned = true`; the first size byte `0xff` then makes `one_byte_size_ready()` choose the eight-byte length path, and the next eight bytes decode to `payload_length = 51200`, hence `msg_size = 51199 > 8192`. The saved ASan trace further proves that a later bad static-buffer read uses `size_ = 8215`. No broader input class is claimed beyond this exact witness and those observed semantics.
